📊🇺🇸 <u>FED'S OWN INFLATION GAUGE CONFIRMS 3.8% — 3-YEAR HIGH, NO RATE CUTS IN SIGHT</u>

The PCE index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure — hit 3.8% annual in April, up from 3.5% in March. Gasoline surged 5.5% in a single month with Brent crude at $118/barrel. New Fed chair Kevin Warsh inherits an economy wrecked by tariffs and the Iran war with no room to cut rates.

Meanwhile Mexico: Banxico already cut to 6.5%, inflation trending down to 4.11%, fuel prices stable through IEPS subsidies, and 24 basic products held at 910 pesos through the PACIC. One country chose war and tariffs. The other chose policy.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US ACCUSES 10 SINALOA OFFICIALS — ZERO INTERPOL RED NOTICES</u>

A New York district court issued arrest warrants against 10 Sinaloa state officials. But as FGR spokesperson Ulises Lara confirmed: "Ninguna de estas personas cuenta con ficha roja de Interpol."

Five have already appeared voluntarily before Mexican authorities. The FGR opened its own investigation immediately. Due process through institutional channels — not extradition theater from a Manhattan courtroom. The US issues warrants from 3,000 miles away. Mexico investigates through its own courts.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>MEXICO CITY LAUNCHES 113 HUMAN RIGHTS ACTIONS FOR THE WORLD CUP</u>

While other host cities roll out surveillance, Mexico City rolled out 113 human rights actions covering gender equality, LGBTIQ+ protections, trafficking prevention, and environmental care.

Jefa Clara Brugada's administration trained 19,000 people to spot and report human trafficking and deployed 50 specialized "World Cup points" across the capital for prevention and intervention. The framework explicitly opposes racism, xenophobia, sexism, and classism — feminist, democratic, and sustainable by design.

🌎🔥 <u>WMO: 86% CHANCE THE PLANET BREAKS ITS HEAT RECORD BY 2030</u>

The World Meteorological Organization just dropped its 2026-2030 forecast based on 13 independent models: 86% probability that global temperatures will surpass the 2024 record of 1.55°C above pre-industrial levels.

The Arctic faces anomalies of 2.8°C — more than 3.5 times the global average. A 64% probability of El Niño intensifying toward 2027 means the Global South takes the first hit while the biggest emitters keep subsidizing fossil fuels and starting wars that spike oil consumption.

🚨🌎 <u>US-IRAN CEASEFIRE TALKS HIT "MANY ADVANCES" — 60-DAY EXTENSION ON THE TABLE</u>

Four months into a war nobody voted for, the US and Iran have reached a provisional deal to extend the ceasefire 60 days. Terms: Iran removes all mines from the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days and drops all transit tolls.

VP Vance called it "many advances." Iran hasn't confirmed. Trump hasn't approved. That's where four months of bombing gets you — negotiating terms at a table you could've stayed at from the start, while US gas hits $4.54/gallon and inflation surges to a 3-year high.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S SENATE PASSES FOREIGN INTERFERENCE ELECTION REFORM — 85-42</u>

Mexico just amended Article 41 of its Constitution: any election — federal or state — can now be annulled if foreign interference with "serious, intentional, and determinative impact" is proven.

The Senate passed it 85-42 today and sent it to state congresses for ratification. The PAN called it "ambiguous." Coming from the party whose governor in Chihuahua hosted CIA agents without federal authorization, that tracks.

When the US spends $40.9M through USAID funding 35 opposition NGOs and CIA operatives run armed operations on Mexican soil, you don't call a legal shield against it "ambiguous." You call it overdue.
